pr_title: Proceed with startup if an integration setup blocks for more than 30m
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

If an integration blocks in `async_setup` or `setup`, Home Assistant will never startup.  You can test this by adding a sleep in `__init__.py` in any integration.

This makes it difficult to figure out which integration is causing the issue because the log message about it taking more than 10s is usually very far away from the end of the log stream and the user does not know which integration is causing the issue especially if there are multiple ones blocking startup.

` Setting up sensor.synology_dsm`

Not sure how to clean that up or if I should.
Probably shouldn't shield from cancellation after 30m best to just cancel. Not sure though as it might actually startup later ?
I suggest we try cancelling it. But I do wonder if a user would ever wait 30 minutes? I guess it's a last line of defense if something goes really bad so that's good.

> I suggest we try cancelling it. But I do wonder if a user would ever wait 30 minutes? I guess it's a last line of defense if something goes really bad so that's good.

I took out the cancelation shield.

I know I've spent way longer than 30 minutes trying to get things up and running when something goes wrong.  I'm definitely thinking of this as a last resort where the user can't figure out the problem but at least their system isn't offline for hours/days/weeks while they are seeking help.
I need to adjust the test to give it time to execute since it now cancels

30 minutes seems a bit long, but maybe we can add some logs after 2m or 5m? Something like "Waiting {x}m for slower integrations to complete setup". When I was debugging my issue there was absolutely nothing in the logs and it seemed that everything had just given up.
I reopened the issue that was linked.  Please keep comments in the issue as we don't want to generate notifications on merged PRs.

issue_context.title: HTTP fails to start if cameras cannot be setup
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->

If there is an issue setting up the camera integration, the HTTP server will fail to load and home assistant will be completely inaccessible.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.110 
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.109.6 
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Docker
- Integration causing this issue: http + camera
- Link to integration documentation on our website: 

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
- platform: generic
  # Note that this camera is currently unplugged, but didn't cause any problems in 0.109.x
  still_image_url: http://192.168.1.96/snap.jpeg
  stream_source: rtsp://192.168.1.60:7447/5de6188051ec9659df33fsdceb6441b2_2
  name: G3 Flex
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt

```

## Additional information

There wouldn't be any errors visible to suggest the problem, I had to go through my integrations one by one to find the culprit. Instead, it would always be in the `starting` state and never complete. Removing the unavailable cameras fixes the issue.

The issue should be reproducible by setting up a generic camera pointing to a URL with a long timeout on it. 

There are similar issues at #35873 and #35888

Hey there @home-assistant/core, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`http`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L181) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
Can confirm that this does indeed happen - quite frustrating as it's very hard to diagnose.

Trial by error I'm afraid. I don't think the issue is specifically the camera integration, I think it's the new setup procedure, it needs to be more tolerant. It seems if any Integration has an issue during the setup, the http module doesn't start.

Yes that's awful when you have around 60 platforms.

I can't even launch 0.109.6 anymore. EDIT: Got 0.109.6 running.

Let me know if I can provide any information, but I've already searched the debug log and haven't found any smoking guns.
I have the same issue since upgrading to 0.110., unfortunately disabling the camera integration didn't help, too many integrations to try manually :frowning_face:
For me, downgrading to 0.109.6 did not fix the problem, I'm starting to get pretty desperate. @ChromoX, how did you get it to work again?

I hope I'm not hijacking this thread with something that is unrelated, but I also have the problem that the http server does not start (not showing up with `ss -tlp`) after upgrade to 0.110, with no error in the log whatsoever. I have tried the following, with no success:

- Downgrade to 0.109.6
- Downgrade to 0.109.2
- Rollback of my entire system (HA Core running in a venv on an RPi 3, Python 3.7.3) to a state where it used to work (with 0.109.2)
- Commenting out everything except `homeassistant` in `configuration.yaml`
- Renaming `.storage`
- Renaming `.storage/core.config_entries`

The only way to bring back the web server/frontend is to intentionally make the `configuration.yaml` invalid. Then, safe mode starts and I can see the frontend.

I'm at a total loss how to proceed and any advice is highly appreciated.

Try

`grep taking home-assistant.log`

Disable any integration that is taking over 10s to startup.

@DavidMStraub I had to remove all custom components and HACS manually going through `.storage` and removing all references. I disabled most integrations and then got 0.109.6 restarting. Then I slowly added all my integrations back.

Honestly it's a little disappointing that HA has been going towards the GUI integrations, yet the HTTP server is not stable enough to deal with misbehaving add-ons. Therefore in some situations it's not possible to disable integrations without having the GUI running it looks like.

Thanks @ChromoX and @bdraco. For whatever reason, my 0.109.2 recovered after a couple of hours. Now I'm unsure if I should attempt another upgrade to 0.110. I'm also unsure if my problem was the same as the issue described here. I agree that removing integrations *without* UI has become more difficult than in old YAML times...

(Originally posted on the PR):

30 minutes seems a bit long, but maybe we can add some logs after 2m or 5m? Something like "Waiting {x}m for slower integrations to complete setup". When I was debugging my issue there was absolutely nothing in the logs and it seemed that everything had just given up.

> (Originally posted on the PR):
> 
> 30 minutes seems a bit long, but maybe we can add some logs after 2m or 5m? Something like "Waiting {x}m for slower integrations to complete setup". When I was debugging my issue there was absolutely nothing in the logs and it seemed that everything had just given up.

Integrations can take a while to install dependencies so we can't cancel them sooner without risking breaking an integration that would actually startup if we gave it enough time. #36082 is more of a fail safe.

We already log when an integration is taking more than 10s to startup.

#36093 has a more substantive change where we made the webserver and frontend available very soon after startup.

I'm not saying they should be cancelled, just they the logging should be improved. There's a massive jump between 10 seconds and 30 minutes, with the user not knowing what's happening in between.

A log on a 1m loop with something like

``` 
Waiting for the following integrations to complete:
- [ ] camera
- [x] rest
- [x] spotify
```

For example would make debugging much better.
However the fix in #36093 would also go a long way in helping.
That would be nice for sure.

I don't think that is actually happening because I see this in the log
```
2020-05-24 17:21:02 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup of component nut is taking longer than 1800 seconds. Startup will proceed without waiting any longer.
2020-05-24 17:21:02 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Unable to prepare setup for platform nut.sensor: Unable to set up component.
```

Pascal is talking about installations that run under the Supervisor. The Supervisor is doing a health check to see if the API is coming online, if so, it marks the upgrade as successful.
However, if the frontend is available via #36093, this wouldn't be an issue.
